🤖 Talos triage · confidence: medium

Talos can make mistakes. Please check important information.

Verdict
Not confirmed as a platform defect, and not "working as designed" either — this monitor produced results for the two previous fiscal periods and produced none for the latest, so something changed and the run record for that monitor is what settles it; no matching known incident.

What we checked

  • Every scheduled run of a monitor is recorded with its outcome and a saved copy of the exact query it ran, so we can tell apart "it ran and found nothing", "it never ran", and "it errored" — none of which look different to the customer, who sees zero either way.

  • The loyalty/stars values this monitor is built on are passed straight through from the data we receive with no transformation or rename on our side, and this monitor's own definition and query are not held in the client configuration files — they live in the application itself, so there is no configuration drift visible from the config repo.

Next

  • Pull the run record for this monitor for the latest fiscal period and for the two periods that worked, and compare: did it complete, did it error, or did it complete having found nothing.

  • Re-run the saved copy of the query from the failing period and from a good period; if the new period genuinely returns nothing, the next check is whether the loyalty/stars values arrived for those trading days.

","created":"2026-09-30T17:54:51.931-0400","updated":"2026-09-30T17:54:51.931-0400","updateAuthor":{"accountId":"712020:74f4ec33-f3c5-4d18-b43e-ff543e20e139","displayName":"Camila Cortes"},"jsdPublic":true},{"id":"3373423","author":{"accountId":"712020:74f4ec33-f3c5-4d18-b43e-ff543e20e139","displayName":"Camila Cortes"},"body":"

Issue: Work item "SFE - Star Farming same day high volume" returned 0 results in the scheduled monthly run for fiscal period 24 Aug–27 Sep 2026. Non-zero results in the prior 2 periods. Customer flagged a possible relation to https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-28873 .

Context: The monitor's definition/query lives in application code, not client config, and confirmed loyalty/stars values pass through from source data unmodified. This client (c166_sbx) cut over from legacy pyardm to SnowTime on 8/27/26 — a date that falls inside this exact failing fiscal period. RCS-28873 documents two Secure field-catalog defects for this client tied to that cutover, both on MemberID/loyalty fields (catalog declared MemberID as Int64; SnowTime's X_MEMBERID is TEXT) — fixed in arpfiles PR #57459, deployed 9/24 — plus a third, still-open application-code bug found 9/25: DeaggregationEngine.cs binds MemberID as an unquoted numeric literal in some query paths, throwing "Numeric value not recognized" for non-numeric-shaped MemberIDs. That fix was not yet deployed as of RCS-28873's last update. Given this monitor is MemberID/loyalty-keyed and the failing period spans the cutover date, this is a stronger candidate explanation than a genuine empty result set.

Steps to review/replicate:

  1. Pull the run record for this monitor for the latest fiscal period and the two prior (good) periods: completed / errored / completed-with-zero for each.

  2. Re-run the saved copy of the query from the failing period and a good period, and check for a swallowed/logged Snowflake numeric-cast error on the run, not just the row count.

  3. Check whether the query aggregates/filters by MemberID and, if so, whether it hits the same unquoted-numeric-bind path documented in RCS-28873.

Next steps: If the query is hitting the DeaggregationEngine numeric-cast bug, this is not a separate defect and needs to be linked to RCS-28873 and loop in Secure engineering rather than opening a new investigation thread. If the query returns genuinely clean with zero matching rows (no error), fall back to checking whether loyalty/stars source data arrived for those trading days. Update customer once determined.

Cause found. The trigger search for this definition fails on every run since the cutover.

Check I ran

Result

SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY, user SVC_ARP_PRODUCTION_166_USER

Query aliased Topic_-SFE-_Star_Farming_same_day_high_volume

Status by day

26 Aug SUCCESS 35. 28 Aug FAIL 4. 9 Sep FAIL 4. 30 Sep FAIL 276. 1 Oct FAIL 180

Last failure

1 Oct 14:05 PT, query ID 01c77251-0109-d5e7-0120-d20111b67fc7

Error, verbatim:

Numeric value '1867074335977200' is not recognized

The condition that fails:

T9.x_MemberID <> 70267962874

Finding. x_MemberID is TEXT in ARDM_PRODUCTION.C166_SBX. The definition compares it to an unquoted numeric literal, so Snowflake casts every MemberID to a number and stops on the first value it cannot convert. The generator retries every 15 minutes and fails each time.

Same error family as the MemberID retype on https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-28873 .

Open question. Did arpfiles PR 57459 cover this definition, or does its condition still carry the Int64 type?

Related: https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-29205 and https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-29206

Escalating to Delivery, Secure 5. The SFE Star Farming same day high volume definition fails on every run since the 27 Aug SnowTime cutover, so no work items generate for fiscal period 24 Aug to 27 Sep. Support cannot change the definition.

1. Environment and steps to reproduce

Prod. Tenant starbucks-us, c166_sbx, ARDM_PRODUCTION.C166_SBX.

Starbucks NA (SBX), reported 30 Sep

  1. Snowflake, SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY, user SVC_ARP_PRODUCTION_166_USER, error_code 100038, from 30 Sep.

  2. Open query ID 01c77251-0109-d5e7-0120-d20111b67fc7, 1 Oct 14:05 PT. Its columns are aliased Topic_-SFE-_Star_Farming_same_day_high_volume.

  3. Executive Workbench, Workview Monitor set to this definition, date range 1 Jul to 1 Oct.

Expected: runs on 1 Jul, 29 Jul, 26 Aug and 30 Sep. Actual: no run on 30 Sep. Error on condition T9.x_MemberID <> 70267962874:

Numeric value '1867074335977200' is not recognized

2. Findings

Detail and run counts by day in my internal note of 1 Oct.

x_MemberID is TEXT in ARDM_PRODUCTION.C166_SBX. This definition compares it to an unquoted number.Sebastian Rueda confirmed on 1 Oct that arpfiles PR 57459 retyped MemberID from Int64 to String. My reading, unverified: this definition's own condition still declares MemberID as Int64, the same pattern StarRewardTransactions.search had on https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-28873 .

3. Troubleshooting performed

Snowflake query history for the service user. Executive Workbench for this definition and for control fiscal period definitions. Teams with Sebastian Rueda on 1 Oct. No other conversations. Support has no access to the definition condition.

4. Still open

  1. Does this definition's condition carry its own Int64 type for MemberID?

  2. Once corrected, can the 24 Aug to 27 Sep run be regenerated?

Related: https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-28873 and https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-29205
